questionTypes.recall: Checks what happened in the story.
questionTypes.comprehension: Checks why it mattered or how one event caused another.
questionTypes.discussion: Opens a family conversation after reading.

questions.question: What mistake did Odysseus and his men make after raiding the Cicones?
questions.answer: They stayed too long instead of leaving quickly.

questions.question: Why does this chapter begin the journey with a hard lesson?
questions.answer: It shows that greed, delay, and not listening can cost lives.

questions.question: Have you ever seen someone win something but then push too far? What would have been wiser?
What did the lotus flowers make some sailors forget?
questions.answer: They forgot their wish to go home.

questions.question: Why was the Lotus-Eaters' island dangerous even though it seemed peaceful?
questions.answer: Its danger was comfort and forgetting, not fighting.

questions.question: What is something pleasant that can still distract people from what matters?
What false name did Odysseus give Polyphemus?
questions.answer: He said his name was Nobody.

questions.question: How did Odysseus' taunting change the rest of the journey?
questions.answer: He revealed his real name, so Polyphemus called on Poseidon to curse him.

questions.question: Odysseus was clever enough to escape, but vain enough to boast. Where have you seen vanity make a problem worse? What would have been a better approach?
What gift did Aeolus give Odysseus?
questions.answer: A bag holding the storm winds.

questions.question: Why did the crew open the bag?
questions.answer: They grew suspicious and thought Odysseus might be hiding treasure.

questions.question: Why can mistrust hurt a group, even when everyone wants to get home?
What happened to most of Odysseus' ships in the Laestrygonian harbor?
questions.answer: They were trapped and destroyed; only Odysseus' ship escaped.

questions.question: Why did Odysseus' choice to anchor outside the harbor matter?
questions.answer: It kept his ship from being trapped with the others.

questions.question: When is caution helpful, even if other people think you are being too careful?
What did Circe do to some of Odysseus' men?
questions.answer: She transformed them into pigs.

questions.question: How did Hermes help Odysseus face Circe?
questions.answer: Hermes gave him protection and advice so Circe's magic would not overpower him.

questions.question: Circe changes from enemy to helper. What can make someone change how they treat others?
Which prophet did Odysseus seek in the Underworld?
questions.answer: Tiresias.

questions.question: Why is the Underworld chapter sad as well as spooky?
questions.answer: Odysseus meets the dead and faces grief, memory, and warnings.

questions.question: Why do stories sometimes ask heroes to listen to hard truths before they can go forward?
How did Odysseus protect his crew from the Sirens?
questions.answer: He had them plug their ears and tie him to the mast.

questions.question: Why was Scylla and Charybdis such a terrible choice?
questions.answer: Both routes were dangerous, so Odysseus had to choose the loss he thought they could survive.

questions.question: Have you ever had to choose between two imperfect options? How did you decide?
Whose sacred cattle did the men kill?
questions.answer: The cattle of Helios, the sun god.

questions.question: Why did this choice bring disaster?
questions.answer: The men broke a divine warning, and Zeus destroyed the ship.

questions.question: Why can hunger, fear, or exhaustion make good rules harder to follow?
Who kept Odysseus on Ogygia?
questions.answer: Calypso.

questions.question: Why did Odysseus choose to leave even though Calypso offered comfort and immortality?
questions.answer: His heart still turned toward his mortal home, family, and real life.

questions.question: Why might a difficult real life be better than an easy life that is not truly yours?
What trick did Penelope use to delay choosing a suitor?
questions.answer: She wove by day and unwove the cloth by night.

questions.question: Why is the palace dangerous even without monsters?
questions.answer: The suitors are consuming Odysseus' house and pressuring Penelope and Telemachus.

questions.question: What kind of courage does Penelope show while she waits?
What disguise did Athena use when she visited Telemachus?
questions.answer: She came as Mentes.

questions.question: What did Athena push Telemachus to do?
questions.answer: Speak against the suitors and travel to seek news of his father.

questions.question: Who helps you become braver when you feel too small for a problem?
Which old king did Telemachus visit in Pylos?
questions.answer: Nestor.

questions.question: What did Telemachus gain even though Nestor did not know where Odysseus was?
questions.answer: Respect, encouragement, and a next step toward Sparta.

questions.question: Why can asking older people for stories or advice matter?
Who hosted Telemachus in Sparta?
questions.answer: Menelaus and Helen.

questions.question: What important hope did Telemachus receive in Sparta?
questions.answer: He learned that Odysseus might still be alive on Calypso's island.

questions.question: How can hope help someone, even before the problem is solved?
Who wrecked Odysseus' raft with a storm?
questions.answer: Poseidon.

questions.question: How did Odysseus survive after the raft broke apart?
questions.answer: He kept swimming, accepted help, and reached the shore of Scheria.

questions.question: What helps people keep going when they are exhausted?
Who found Odysseus near the river on Scheria?
questions.answer: Nausicaa.

questions.question: Why are the Phaeacians important to Odysseus' return?
questions.answer: Their hospitality gives him safety, a listening audience, and passage home.

questions.question: What makes someone a good host to a stranger?
Who disguised Odysseus as a beggar when he reached Ithaca?
questions.answer: Athena.

questions.question: Why did Odysseus not reveal himself immediately?
questions.answer: He needed to learn what was happening in his house and who could be trusted.

questions.question: When is it wise to watch and listen before acting?
Where did Odysseus reveal himself to Telemachus?
questions.answer: In Eumaeus' hut.

questions.question: Why is this reunion more than just a happy moment?
questions.answer: Father and son also become allies who must plan how to reclaim the house.

questions.question: How can family members become teammates when something is hard?
Which old dog recognized Odysseus?
questions.answer: Argos.

questions.question: Why is Odysseus' disguise painful inside his own palace?
questions.answer: He sees his home mistreated while he must stay hidden and endure insults.

questions.question: What is hard about being patient when someone treats you unfairly?
What challenge did Penelope set for the suitors?
questions.answer: String Odysseus' bow and shoot through the axes.

questions.question: Why did the bow prove who Odysseus was?
questions.answer: It was tied to his strength, skill, and old life in the house.

questions.question: Why are some tests better than just asking someone to say who they are?
What did Odysseus reveal after shooting through the axes?
questions.answer: He revealed that he was the true master of the house.

questions.question: Why is this chapter serious rather than simply exciting?
questions.answer: It brings justice and danger together, and the violence has consequences.

questions.question: What is the difference between justice and revenge?
What secret did Penelope use to test Odysseus?
questions.answer: The marriage bed built around a living olive tree.

questions.question: Why was Penelope right to be careful?
questions.answer: She had survived for years by testing words and not trusting too quickly.

questions.question: How can caution be a form of wisdom instead of fear?
Which goddess helped stop the cycle of revenge in Ithaca?
questions.answer: Athena.

questions.question: Why does the story need peace after Odysseus wins back his house?
questions.answer: The families of the suitors are angry, and Ithaca needs healing instead of more violence.

questions.question: What does it take for people to stop fighting after everyone has been hurt?
